title: Build a transactional outbox and relay
prompt:
When a booking is confirmed, the ticket site must save it and publish a booking.confirmed event (email, ticket PDF and analytics all listen). Doing db.save() then broker.publish() is a dual write: a crash between them loses the event. The fix is the transactional outbox.

A small InMemoryDb with real all-or-nothing transactions is provided at the top of the editor. Implement:

  • placeBooking(db, booking): in one db.transaction, insert the booking into bookings (with status: 'confirmed') and a row into outbox: { id: 'evt_' + booking.id, topic: 'booking.confirmed', payload: { bookingId, seatId, amountCents } }.
  • class OutboxRelay with new OutboxRelay({ db, publish, clock }) and async runOnce(limit = 100): read db.unsentOutbox(limit) (oldest first), and for each row await publish({ id, topic, payload }) then db.markSent(id, clock.now()). If publish or markSent throws, stop this run (so events stay in order) and return normally. Return how many rows were published and marked.
placeBooking(db, { id: 'b1', seatId: '14C', amountCents: 8900 });
await relay.runOnce();   // publishes { id: 'evt_b1', topic: 'booking.confirmed', ... }, returns 1
await relay.runOnce();   // nothing left, returns 0

tests.name: booking and outbox row are written together
a failed commit leaves neither the booking nor the event
relay publishes in order, marks sent with the injected clock, and does not resend
broker down: nothing is lost, the next run delivers everything
a mid-batch failure stops the run so order is preserved
respects the batch limit
crash after publish but before markSent: redelivered with the same id (at-least-once)

hints: placeBooking: add a second tx.insert('outbox', {...}) inside the same callback. Because both inserts go through the same tx, the provided DB commits both or neither.
runOnce: loop over this.db.unsentOutbox(limit). Wrap publish + markSent for one row in a try; in the catch, break out of the loop instead of throwing.

Shape:

let n = 0;
for (const row of this.db.unsentOutbox(limit)) {
  try {
    await this.publish({ id: row.id, topic: row.topic, payload: row.payload });
    this.db.markSent(row.id, this.clock.now());
    n++;
  } catch (e) { break; }
}
return n;
explain:
This is the transactional outbox pattern. In production the outbox is a real table in the same Postgres (or MySQL) database as your business data, and the relay is either a poller like this one (often SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so several relays can share the work) or change data capture (CDC), e.g. Debezium reading the database's write-ahead log and pushing rows to Kafka.

Notice the last test: the outbox gives you at-least-once delivery, never exactly-once. The stable event id is what lets every consumer dedupe, which is how you get effectively-once processing.

Say it in the interview: "I won't dual-write to the database and the broker. The booking and its event go into the same transaction via an outbox table; a relay or CDC publishes from there. Delivery is at-least-once, so events carry a stable id and consumers are idempotent."
